## My request for Codex:
Production-ready implementation roadmap for the full X3 blockchain plan
Executive summary

This report turns the user’s X3 roadmap into a production-grade build plan that unifies: TPS fixes (txpool, 200ms blocks, batch sig verify, parallel proposer), single-round finality (Flash Finality), PoH-style ordering, Atomic Execution Kernel + PoAE, shared sequencer/settlement/DA, GPU swarm integration, and desktop hardening. It is written to be actionable as a sequence of PRs with clear acceptance criteria, deterministic safety constraints, and rollback levers.

Primary connected sources used first (as requested): GitHub and DataCamp; prioritized repo: Cyptopimpinainteazy/atlas-sphere. Key repo anchors include the node service file for txpool/proposer/finality wiring, runtime constants, and the desktop Tauri security configuration.

The highest-impact “day-one” fixes are:

    Raise Substrate txpool limits (default ready=8192/future=512 is far too small for high-load; default ban_time is long).
    Halve block time to 200ms (with a runtime spec bump and weight tuning).
    Desktop: remove broad Shell capabilities and eliminate unsafe-eval from CSP to reduce renderer→RCE blast radius, following Tauri’s CSP/capabilities guidance and known shell plugin risk history.
    Fix the Orderbook launcher regression by aligning app registry IDs (dex-orderbook).

Baseline and design principles

The repo already encodes two important design constraints that should be treated as non-negotiable for production:

Determinism-first parallelism: the repo’s predictive parallel execution proposal explicitly requires a “parallel == serial state root” invariant and a forced fallback to serial execution under low confidence. This is the correct production posture: ML predictions can be a hint, not a consensus rule.

Finality integration must follow Substrate’s “block import onion” model: Substrate finality gadgets (e.g., GRANDPA) integrate by wrapping the block import pipeline and spawning a long-running voter task; blocks must pass through the wrapper or consensus breaks in “unexpected ways.” Flash Finality must copy this integration contract.

Two external reference “templates” are useful to keep you honest:

    HotStuff / Sync HotStuff for leader-driven voting and certificate formation (while being mindful that real-world implementations frequently fail on concurrency/edge cases).
    Solana’s published PoH / Turbine / Gulf Stream / Sealevel principles as inspiration, especially the “declare what you touch” model for safe parallel scheduling.

Key technical designs
Transaction pool tuning in node/src/service.rs

Substrate’s sc_transaction_pool::Options defaults are ready.count=8192, ready.total_bytes=20MB, future.count=512, future.total_bytes=1MB, and ban_time=30 minutes. At high TPS, those defaults are a self-inflicted bottleneck.

Design choice (open but recommended): set large count limits and raise total_bytes enough to hold multiple blocks worth of transactions during bursts; keep ban_time short enough to allow retries after transient failures. The txpool’s ready/future split and nonce dependency model makes future-queue sizing particularly important when you have many concurrent senders with nonce gaps.

Concrete patch example (illustrative diff):

diff

diff --git a/node/src/service.rs b/node/src/service.rs
@@ fn new_full(...) -> Result<...> {
-  let transaction_pool = sc_transaction_pool::BasicPool::new_full(
-      config.transaction_pool.clone(),
-      is_authority.into(),
-      prometheus_registry.as_ref(),
-      task_manager.spawn_handle(),
-      client.clone(),
-  );
+  // High-throughput tuning (production defaults; can be overridden via CLI later).
+  // Default Substrate limits are small (ready=8192, future=512). citeturn1search2
+  let pool_options = sc_transaction_pool::Options {
+      ready: sc_transaction_pool::PoolLimit {
+          count: 100_000,
+          total_bytes: 256 * 1024 * 1024, // 256MB
+      },
+      future: sc_transaction_pool::PoolLimit {
+          count: 50_000,
+          total_bytes: 64 * 1024 * 1024, // 64MB
+      },
+      reject_future_transactions: false,
+      ban_time: std::time::Duration::from_secs(120), // 2 minutes
+  };
+
+  let transaction_pool = sc_transaction_pool::BasicPool::new_full(
+      pool_options,
+      is_authority.into(),
+      prometheus_registry.as_ref(),
+      task_manager.spawn_handle(),
+      client.clone(),
+  );

Acceptance tests for this PR:

    A load test that previously saturated the pool must show stable PoolStatus (ready/future counts and bytes) behavior and no runaway banning loops.
    Verify memory usage under worst-case pool fill and that OOM is not possible on target validator hardware.

200ms blocks in runtime/src/lib.rs

Reducing block time is a runtime change: you must bump spec_version and treat it as a runtime upgrade, with appropriate migration/rollout. Substrate digest/header types and proposer deadlines depend on runtime timing constants.

Concrete patch example:

diff

diff --git a/runtime/src/lib.rs b/runtime/src/lib.rs
@@
-pub const MILLISECS_PER_BLOCK: u64 = 400;
+pub const MILLISECS_PER_BLOCK: u64 = 200;
@@
 pub const VERSION: RuntimeVersion = RuntimeVersion {
@@
-  spec_version: 2,
+  // Runtime upgrade required due to block time change.
+  spec_version: 3,
   impl_version: 1,

Production requirement: retune BlockWeights (and EVM gas limits if applicable) so that import time remains < block time on commodity validator machines, or you will “win” at authoring and lose at validation.
Parallel proposer crate and integration

Substrate’s block production hooks are defined by sp_consensus::Environment and sp_consensus::Proposer. A custom proposer must obey the same API contract as sc_basic_authorship::ProposerFactory.

A production-grade crates/parallel-proposer should expose:

    A factory implementing Environment<Block> that returns a proposer which:
        Pulls ready txs from the pool.
        Computes (or reads) per-tx access metadata.
        Uses ML predictor output as a hint only, and then enforces deterministic conflict rules.
        Executes shards in parallel in isolated overlays, merges deterministically, and falls back to serial when conflicts are detected or metadata is missing.

Deterministic access metadata strategy:

    For “parallel-eligible” extrinsics (AtomicBundle submissions, sequencer batch finalizations), require a declared access list (read/write) as part of the extrinsic payload. This copies the production-proven Solana constraint: transactions must declare which accounts they read/write to allow safe parallel scheduling.
    For legacy extrinsics without declared access, treat as “global write” (forces serialization).

Mermaid sequence for proposer + predictor + deterministic scheduler:

Executor (CPU/GPU)DeterministicSchedulerContentionPredictorTxPoolProposerExecutor (CPU/GPU)DeterministicSchedulerContentionPredictorTxPoolProposerpar[shard execution]ready_transactions()tx listpredict_shards(tx_metadata)suggested shard groups (+confidence)build_shards(tx, suggestions)conflict-free shards + serial-fallback setexecute(shard_0 overlay)execute(shard_1 overlay)shard diffsdeterministic_merge(diffs)merged overlay OR conflict -> fallback serial

This matches the repo’s own “fallback to serial on low confidence” invariant expectations.
Flash Finality crate: message format and Substrate wiring

HotStuff provides a clear template for leader proposal + quorum votes + certificate, and Sync HotStuff shows practical high-throughput in synchronous settings; but implementation pitfalls are well-documented, so the plan must include shadow mode, fuzzing, and kill switches.

Minimal message formats (binary SCALE encoding recommended):

    Proposal { block_hash, slot, round, leader_id, leader_sig }
    Vote { block_hash, slot, round, voter_id, voter_sig }
    Certificate { block_hash, slot, round, signers: Vec<(id, sig)> }

Signature approach (open choice, recommended staging):

    v0: Ed25519 multisig as (id, sig) tuples; verify in batch (GPU-fast, CPU-fallback).
    v1: BLS aggregation once stable, if you want smaller certificates.

Substrate integration pattern to copy:

    Create a FlashFinalityBlockImport wrapper (analogous to GRANDPA’s wrapper).
    Spawn a long-running “voter” task (analogous to run_grandpa_voter) that:
        Tracks best chain head.
        Participates in vote collection for the current leader.
        Emits finality notifications when certificates verify.

Shadow-mode production tactic:

    Keep GRANDPA running while Flash Finality runs “observe and certificate” but doesn’t mark final until it matches GRANDPA for N hours/days on testnet.
    Once stable, switch finality source by feature flag.

PoH generator: digest format and verification

Solana’s whitepaper establishes PoH as a verifiable time-order mechanism and explicitly discusses GPU-based signature verification throughput and batching concepts.

In Substrate, PoH belongs in digest items (DigestItem::PreRuntime or Consensus), with a stable engine ID. Digest types are explicitly part of the generic header model.

Proposed digest payload (SCALE):

    PohDigestV1 { start_tick: u64, end_tick: u64, poh_hash: [u8;32], mixed_tx_hashes: Vec<[u8;32]> }

Verification rule:

    Validators re-derive the PoH chain for the declared tx hash sequence and verify poh_hash.
    If verification fails: reject proposal / refuse vote (Flash Finality).

pallets/x3-atomic-kernel: skeleton and lifecycle

The Atomic Kernel pallet is the on-chain coordination layer. It does not have to execute every leg on-chain; the production strategy is: store bundles, enforce deterministic access rules, verify legs/proofs (GPU-accelerated where possible), and commit final state updates deterministically.

Core types (FRAME-friendly, SCALE encodable):

    AtomicBundle { bundle_id, source_chain, legs, checkpoints, deadline, proof_type, declared_access }
    AtomicLeg { leg_id, vm_type, source_chain, target_chain, payload, gas_limit, access_hint, proof }
    ProofType { ZeroKnowledge, Optimistic }

Storage:

    AtomicBundles: map bundle_id => AtomicBundle
    AtomicBundleStatus: map bundle_id => (status, legs_completed, final_state_root, finalized_at)
    AtomicAccessLocks: map key => bundle_id (optional for enforcement)
    AtomicSettlements: map bundle_id => record

Dispatchables:

    execute_atomic_bundle(origin, bundle) → stores + emits BundleSubmitted.
    finalize_atomic_bundle(origin, bundle_id, proofs) → verifies proofs, computes final root, emits BundleFinalized.
    rollback_atomic_bundle(origin, bundle_id, failed_leg_index) → restores from checkpoint / marks rolled back.

Events:

    BundleSubmitted { bundle_id }
    BundleFinalized { bundle_id, final_state_root }
    BundleRolledBack { bundle_id, failed_leg_index }

Errors:

    BundleNotFound
    InvalidBundle
    DeadlineExceeded
    GpuVerificationFailed
    ConflictDetected
    NoCheckpointFound

GPU hostcall integration points:

    Batch verify: group legs by VM/proof type; pass batched payloads/proofs to GPU verify hostcall.
    Batch commit: commit batched legs through GPU commit hostcall. Fallback strategy:
    If GPU unavailable, use CPU verify (slower) but identical semantics; never change validity rules by hardware availability.

PoAE proof structure and offchain signing flow

Instead of collecting new signatures per bundle, a production-grade approach is to leverage the consensus finality certificate as the “2/3 signatures” artifact and prove bundle inclusion via a kernel-specific merkle root embedded in the block header.

Proof fields:

    bundle_id
    final_state_root
    block_number, block_hash
    atomic_root (a per-block merkle root over finalized bundles, added as digest)
    bundle_merkle_proof (path in the atomic_root merkle tree)
    finality_certificate (Flash Finality certificate or GRANDPA justification during transition)

This is conceptually aligned with Substrate’s general “justification proves finality for a header” model.
Atomic RPC registration

Substrate nodes typically merge RPC modules into the node’s RpcModule. Registration must happen in service.rs to connect client/backend/txpool handles.

RPC surface (jsonrpsee):

    atomic_submitAtomicBundle(bundle) -> {bundle_id, estimated_finality_ms, status}
    atomic_getBundleStatus(bundle_id) -> status
    atomic_getAtomicExecutionProof(bundle_id) -> proof
    atomic_simulateAtomicBundle(bundle) -> simulation_result
    atomic_subscribeBundleFinalized() -> stream

Acceptance criteria:

    RPC versioning (v1, v2) baked into method names or params.
    Backcompat tests for clients.

Shared sequencer, settlement, and DA pallets

Sequencer pallet:

    submit_transaction(SequencedTx) stores tx in pending batch.
    On finalization, compute batch_merkle_root, store SequencingBatch, emit BatchFinalized.
    Fees: enforce minimum fee + optionally per-byte fee to avoid DA abuse.

Settlement pallet:

    register_rollup(RollupConfig)
    submit_state_root(RollupStateRoot)
    ZK path: verify immediately (reuse verifier infrastructure where possible).
    Optimistic path: store + challenge window + finalize.

DA pallet (production incremental plan):

    v0: store blob hash + metadata on-chain; store actual blob offchain (p2p + archival nodes).
    v1: add Reed-Solomon encoding and shard distribution incentives, inspired by Turbine’s erasure coding + stake-aware dissemination.
    v2: add KZG commitments if Ethereum-style proof compatibility is required.

External client libraries and Solidity bridge

Client library design:

    Provide typed bundle builders.
    Provide subscription helpers for finalization events.
    Provide proof verification helpers.

Solidity interface (minimal):

    submitAtomicBundle(AtomicBundle bundle) returns (bytes32 bundleId)
    getAtomicExecutionProof(bytes32 bundleId) returns (AtomicExecutionProof proof)
    verify(proof) returns (bool) (implementation-specific; may verify merkle + signatures)

Determinism, security, and economics
Deterministic parallel execution model

The production rule is simple: parallelism must never change consensus outputs.

Mechanism:

    Parallel-eligible txs must carry a declared access set (read/write), similar to Solana’s requirement that instructions specify accounts and whether they are writable; only non-overlapping writable sets can run in parallel.
    The ML predictor suggests shards, but deterministic conflict checking verifies shard validity.
    Deterministic merge rules:
        If two overlays attempt to write the same key: reject parallel plan and rerun serial.
        If any tx omits access declaration: force serial.
    Tests:
        Property test: random batches, compare state_root(parallel) vs state_root(serial) across thousands of seeds.
        Replay tests: recorded block traces, parallel builder reproduces canonical roots.

This mirrors the repo’s own explicit invariants for predictive execution.
Desktop hardening: Tauri CSP and capabilities

Your current desktop config is explicitly high risk:

    CSP includes unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval, and has extremely broad connect-src / frame-src wildcards.
    Capabilities grant shell:allow-open, shell:allow-spawn, shell:allow-execute, shell:allow-stdin-write.

That combination is exactly the “renderer compromise → system command execution” chain Tauri warns against: CSP should be as restricted as possible, and shell permissions should be allowlisted to specific commands/args only.

Additionally, the shell plugin has had real-world “open endpoint scope validation” vulnerabilities (CVE/GHSA references), making it even more important to avoid broad shell permissions unless absolutely required.

Concrete patch example for apps/x3-desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json:

diff

diff --git a/apps/x3-desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json b/apps/x3-desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json
@@
   "permissions": [
@@
-    "shell:default",
-    "shell:allow-open",
-    "shell:allow-spawn",
-    "shell:allow-execute",
-    "shell:allow-stdin-write",
+    // Remove broad shell permissions; re-add only scoped allowlists if proven necessary.
+    // Prefer opener plugin for URL opening; shell plugin has a history of "open" scope issues. citeturn5search9turn5search4
+    "opener:default",

If you truly need shell execution (try very hard not to), use Tauri v2 scoped allowlists by command name and argument validators.

Concrete CSP tightening example for apps/x3-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:

diff

diff --git a/apps/x3-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json b/apps/x3-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json
@@
-    "security": {
-      "csp": "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; ...; frame-src 'self' http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*; child-src ...; worker-src 'self' blob:"
-    },
+    "security": {
+      "csp": "default-src 'self' asset:; \
+script-src 'self'; \
+style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; \
+img-src 'self' asset: blob: data:; \
+font-src 'self' asset:; \
+connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost https://rpc.x3-chain.io wss://rpc.x3-chain.io; \
+frame-src 'none'; \
+child-src 'none'; \
+object-src 'none'; \
+base-uri 'self';"
+    },

Rationale: Tauri’s CSP guidance explicitly recommends avoiding remote scripts and keeping CSP restricted, and web security guidance treats unsafe-eval as a major footgun.

CI guardrail (required):

    Add a workflow that fails if:
        shell:allow-execute|spawn|stdin-write appears without an allowlist scope.
        CSP contains unsafe-eval in production builds.

Runtime economic model for GPU executors

Production economics are where high-throughput systems usually die. Minimum requirements:

    Executors (GPU nodes) must stake.
    Jobs must have explicit pricing and deterministic SLA measurement.
    Payout must require redundancy (f-of-n matching results) and/or cryptographic proofs.
    Slashing must be automatic on provable misbehavior (invalid proofs, inconsistent results, downtime).

The “redundancy first” rule mirrors the core consensus lesson: do not trust a single fast box, even if it has a big GPU.

200ms block overload	high	medium	weight retune; perf budget gates	runtime upgrade rollback
GPU path correctness	high	medium	CPU fallback, differential testing	force CPU-only mode
Desktop renderer→RCE	critical	medium	CSP tightening + remove shell exec	block release via CI policy
DA spam / storage blowup	high	high	per-byte fees; size caps; offchain storage	disable DA extrinsics

The roadmap’s critical path (consensus + determinism + kernel proofs) is realistically a multi-month effort even with strong engineers, because finality and determinism work must be proven under adversarial conditions, not just “works on my machine.” X3 Chain Production Roadmap to Outrun Solana
Executive summary

I used the enabled connectors GitHub and DataCamp first, prioritizing the selected repo Cyptopimpinainteazy/atlas-sphere via the connected GitHub tool access (the repo appears not publicly crawlable from my web tool, so I treat repo-specific details as implementation targets and keep public citations focused on primary/official references). I then grounded the plan in primary sources: Substrate/Polkadot SDK Rustdocs for proposer/txpool/finality/digests, official Solana design docs for Turbine/Gulf Stream/Sealevel parallelism, and official Tauri security guidance plus a concrete Shell-plugin advisory for desktop hardening.

The fastest path to “faster than Solana” is not to cosplay every Solana subsystem—it’s to adopt the principles that actually move the needle and integrate them cleanly into Substrate:

    Deterministic parallel execution based on explicit state access declarations (Solana-style “declare reads/writes up front”) rather than ML guesses; ML stays a hint only.
    GPU-batched cryptography in the critical path and consensus-safe with CPU fallback. The Solana whitepaper explicitly calls out batching intrinsic crypto (example: ECDSA) to run in parallel on GPUs and cites dramatic throughput improvement from batching.
    Single-round / two-phase BFT finality inspired by HotStuff/Sync HotStuff families, implemented as a Substrate finality gadget (like GRANDPA integration does today), with tight message formats and clear pacemaker rules—because partially synchronous pacemakers can be attacked if sloppy.
    PoH-like ordering as a verifiable ordering signal embedded in block digests (Substrate digest items), reducing coordination overhead and enabling fast confirmation logic.
    Turbine-like propagation (erasure-coded shreds + tree fanout) but implemented cautiously; Solana’s own outage report shows block forwarding/proxy layers can amplify Turbine load if they mishandle oversized blocks.
    Desktop security hardening: stop enabling broad shell execution + permissive CSP simultaneously; this is a classic “renderer compromise → RCE” combo, and the Tauri team has a concrete plugin-shell advisory demonstrating how subtle scope validation issues can become RCE if you pass untrusted input.

If you execute the roadmap below in the stated order, you get measurable throughput uplift early (txpool + 200ms blocks + deterministic parallel proposer + GPU verification), while keeping the more exotic parts (Turbine/Gulf Stream, shared DA) behind feature gates and safety tests.
Scope and assumptions
Assumptions I’m making because you did not constrain them

    Validator count: unconstrained (I design for 7–200+).
    Network: permissionless mainnet eventually, but staged canary first.
    X3 Kernel: exists and is treated as the canonical execution engine for X3VM + cross-VM operations, with GPU validation hooks and CPU fallback.
    “Faster than Solana” definition: finalized throughput and atomic-bundle finality for the target workload (atomic cross-VM bundles), not synthetic “raw TPS” without finality or without execution.

Non-goals (for clarity)

    Replacing Substrate wholesale. The plan is to evolve a Substrate node/runtime into a high-performance, atomic-execution hub using proven integration points (txpool options, proposer replacement, finality gadget integration patterns, digest items).

Determinism-first parallelism (the “Sealevel lesson” without copying Solana)

Solana’s parallelism works because transactions declare what accounts they read/write, enabling the runtime to schedule non-overlapping transactions concurrently.

For X3, the key choice is:

    Every extrinsic that wants parallel execution MUST include an explicit access list (read/write keys) supported by a runtime trait.
    The “contention predictor” (ML) can propose sharding, but the block must be built using a deterministic conflict check against declared access sets. ML is advisory only.

This guards you from consensus splits where two nodes’ ML inference differs.
Finality approach

GRANDPA is integrated into Substrate as a block import wrapper + a long-running voter task (run_grandpa_voter), and its justifications are a standard sync artifact.

Your Flash Finality should follow the same integration shape, but with HotStuff/Sync HotStuff-inspired two-phase certificates, and very explicit pacemaker behaviors because view timers are a known HotStuff-family liveness hazard if implemented naively.
PoH approach

The Solana whitepaper frames PoH as a mechanism to cryptographically verify passage of time and ordering, and it explicitly links PoH to reducing messaging overhead for fast finality when used alongside consensus.

In Substrate, this maps cleanly onto adding a consensus digest item (DigestItem::PreRuntime or DigestItem::Consensus) containing PoH state per block.
GPU approach

The Solana whitepaper explicitly describes batching crypto “intrinsics” (example: ECDSA verification) and running them on GPUs for large throughput improvements.

Your plan should treat GPU as:

    A performance accelerator (fast path),
    Never a consensus dependency without CPU-verifiable equivalence.

Core component designs
Parallel proposer crate (crates/parallel-proposer)

Substrate requires a sp_consensus::Proposer implementation with propose(args: ProposeArgs).

Design:

    ParallelProposerFactory: implements sp_consensus::Environment, wraps base sc_basic_authorship::ProposerFactory for scaffolding.
    ParallelProposer: implements Proposer, but inside propose():
        Collect ready transactions from pool
        Extract declared access sets from signed extension (required for parallel path)
        Build conflict graph deterministically (RW conflicts)
        Color graph / shard into independent groups
        Execute each group in parallel
        Merge results deterministically (see determinism section)
        If any tx missing access declaration → run it in serial lane (or reject based on policy)

Integration point (node/src/service.rs):

    Replace sc_basic_authorship::ProposerFactory::new with parallel_proposer::ParallelProposerFactory::new, mirroring ProposerFactory usage patterns.

Flash finality crate (crates/flash-finality)

Follow GRANDPA integration shape: block import wrapper + long-running voter task + network notifications.

Message formats (SCALE encodable):

    Proposal { block_hash, block_number, slot, poh_hash, leader_sig }
    Vote { block_hash, block_number, slot, poh_hash, voter_id, voter_sig }
    Certificate { block_hash, block_number, slot, poh_hash, aggregated_sig_or_multisig, bitset }

Protocol:

    leader = Aura author for slot
    vote window = 100–150ms (tunable)
    quorum = 2f+1 out of 3f+1
    pacemaker = view/slot-based; MUST defend against timer manipulation

Why this family: HotStuff highlights leader-based BFT with linearity/responsiveness; Sync HotStuff shows a simple two-phase synchronous approach with 2Δ steady-state latency under synchrony assumptions.
Caution: timer doubling/view sync is a known liveness attack surface; implement pacemaker carefully and test adversarially.
PoH generator crate (crates/poh-generator) and digest format

PoH definition: sequential computation that lets you verify ordering and passage of time; Solana uses SHA-based chained hashing to create an ordering clock.

Digest embedding:

    Use DigestItem::PreRuntime(ENGINE_ID, encoded_poh) or DigestItem::Consensus(...) (engine ID is 4 bytes). Substrate digest items are explicitly defined (PreRuntime / Consensus / Seal / Other).

Proposed encoded payload:

    PohDigestV1 { tick_height: u64, poh_hash: [u8;32], mix_hash: [u8;32], tx_root: [u8;32] }

Rules:

    every block MUST include PoH digest
    PoH hash must be verifiable from previous state + included mixes

pallets/x3-atomic-kernel skeleton (Atomic Execution Kernel)

This pallet is the unified interface, while x3-kernel remains the canonical executor. The atomic kernel:

    performs bundle admission control + accounting
    orchestrates execution via x3-kernel
    stores checkpoints / rollback state
    emits events and supports proofs via PoAE

Core types:

    AtomicBundle, AtomicLeg, Checkpoint, ExecutionStatus
    storage: AtomicBundles, AtomicSettlements, BundleStatus, ExecutorBonds

Core calls:

    submit_bundle(bundle)
    finalize_bundle(bundle_id, execution_receipt)
    rollback_bundle(bundle_id, failed_leg)

Events:

    BundleSubmitted, BundleExecuting, BundleFinalized, BundleRolledBack

Errors:

    BundleNotFound, InvalidBundle, DeadlineExceeded, ProofInvalid, ExecutorUnauthorized, GpuVerificationFailed

PoAE proof structure and signing flow

Baseline: GRANDPA produces justifications that include commits + ancestry proofs and are used to prove finality across the network.

Your PoAE should bind:

    Bundle inclusion (Merkle proof under a per-block bundle root)
    Finality (Flash Finality certificate OR GRANDPA justification during transition)
    Execution receipt hash (produced by x3-kernel execution)

AtomicExecutionProof:

    bundle_id
    block_number, block_hash
    bundle_root, merkle_proof
    execution_receipt_hash
    finality_certificate (Flash cert bytes; during migration accept GRANDPA justifications as alt)
    timestamp

Offchain signing flow:

    On BundleFinalized, node builds proof_hash = H(bundle_id || execution_receipt_hash || block_hash || bundle_root)
    Validators sign via keystore
    Certificate assembled and exposed over RPC

Atomic RPC module registration in node/src/service.rs

Follow standard Substrate node pattern: create RPC module and merge. Keep atomic RPC behind feature flags until stable.
Sequencer / settlement / DA pallets + RPCs

Design picks directly from Solana principles:

    Sequencer: deterministic ordering, Merkle batch roots
    DA: erasure coding like Turbine uses Reed-Solomon to survive packet loss; Solana’s Turbine articles describe shreds + Reed-Solomon codes and stake-weighted trees.

But: roll out DA cautiously. Solana’s outage report shows how malformed forwarding layers can overload Turbine and degrade finalization.
GPU hostcall integration and CPU fallback

Principles:

    every GPU fast path has a CPU path that produces identical acceptance results
    treat GPU as “accelerator,” not “oracle”

Evidence that batching crypto is a major lever:

    Solana whitepaper explicitly: batched intrinsics (example ECDSA verification) on GPU; and it discusses GPU-based ECDSA verification servers achieving high ops/sec and batching intrinsics on GPU.

For EdDSA batch verification optimization research:

    modern cryptographic engineering literature continues to optimize batch verification methods (example: EdDSA speedups and batch method improvements).

Deterministic parallel execution model
Access-set/read-write-set extraction

I recommend adopting a Solana-like explicit declaration model:

    Each extrinsic includes AccessList { reads: Vec<Key>, writes: Vec<Key> } via a signed extension.
    Keys can be:
        Substrate storage keys (hashed prefix)
        X3 Kernel “canonical ledger” keys
        EVM/SVM account abstractions mapped into canonical keys

Why: Solana’s parallelism is enabled because transactions specify up front what state they read/write, allowing parallel scheduling.
Predictor usage (hint-only)

    Contention predictor provides proposed shard grouping.
    Final grouping is computed deterministically by:
        building conflict graph from declared RW sets
        performing deterministic graph coloring/partitioning

Deterministic merge & fallback

    Each shard executes against the same parent state snapshot.
    Writes must be disjoint by construction; if not, scheduler must:
        either merge by a deterministic tie-break rule (NOT recommended for finance)
        or degrade to serial execution for conflicting group

Tests to prove determinism

    Property test: two nodes with same tx list but different predictor outputs must produce identical block/state root.
    Fuzz: random access lists + random call order → verify deterministic results.
    “Poisoned predictor” test: predictor returns invalid sharding; block builder must still be correct.

Security hardening
Desktop hardening for Tauri

Tauri explicitly positions CSP as a key mitigation for XSS and recommends restricting CSP as much as possible, relying on Tauri’s build-time injection of hashes/nonces.
Tauri also provides a capabilities + command scope system intended for granular allow/deny behavior.

The “don’t do this in production” combo:

    permissive CSP (unsafe-eval, broad wildcards)
    broad shell permissions (execute/spawn/stdin-write)

Why I’m blunt about it:

    The Tauri Shell plugin has a real advisory (GHSA-c9pr-q8gx-3mgp) where scope validation issues allowed dangerous protocols like file:// to be opened, which can be abused toward RCE if untrusted input reaches the shell endpoint or if frontend code execution occurs.

Runtime economic model for executors and GPU swarm

Core concepts:

    Executor bond: submitter/executor stakes collateral; slashed for provable faults.
    Redundant execution requirement for GPU jobs: require ≥2 independent GPU nodes to agree on result hash for consensus-critical lanes.
    Job rate limiting per executor identity to prevent “GPU DoS.”

Kill-switches:

    DisableGpuFastPath: force CPU verification
    DisableParallelExecution: force serial proposer
    DisableExternalSequencing: sequencer RPC off

CI checks (desktop):

    Fail CI if shell:allow-execute is present without a scoped allowlist
    Fail CI if CSP contains unsafe-eval without an explicit allowlisted justification and security review tag

Testing, benchmarking, rollout, and risk register
Testing matrix and benchmarks

Benchmarks to add:

    Txpool: sustained submission with 1k–100k tx burst; track PoolStatus and rejection events.
    Proposer: determinism tests + throughput tests by conflict rate (0%, 10%, 50%, 90%)
    GPU: CPU/GPU differential correctness tests; induce GPU failures and verify fallback
    Finality: multi-node (7, 21, 51) with byzantine simulation; check safety/liveness
    E2E: external chain proof verification tests (Solidity + Rust client)

Metrics to collect:

    block build latency P50/P95
    finalized TPS (application tx only)
    finality latency P50/P95
    conflict rate
    GPU utilization and fallback rate
    proof generation latency / size

Rollout and rollback plan

Rollout pattern:

    Phase gates behind runtime constants + node flags
    Canary validators (5–10) on a canary chain
    Upgrade path:
        txpool tuning + metrics
        200ms blocks (runtime upgrade)
        parallel proposer behind flag
        GPU fast path behind flag
        flash finality optional alongside GRANDPA, then cutover
        atomic kernel + PoAE proofs
        sequencer/DA optional services
        GPU swarm economics last

Rollback:

    keep GRANDPA codepath available until flash finality proves stable (Substrate GRANDPA integration is well understood; removing it prematurely is risky).
    to rollback flash finality: disable gadget, re-enable GRANDPA voter tasks
    to rollback parallelism: force serial proposer

Risk register (high-impact items)
Risk	Why it matters	Mitigation	Kill-switch
Parallelism causes state divergence	chain split	deterministic access lists + merge rules + invariant tests	disable parallel proposer
Finality liveness bugs	stalled chain	strict pacemaker tests; adversarial timing tests; reference HotStuff/Sync HS	revert to GRANDPA
GPU nondeterminism	consensus failure	GPU as hint/accelerator only; always CPU-verifiable	disable GPU
DA/Turbine overload	finality degradation	size limits; shred validation; no “smart forwarding proxies”	disable DA propagation
Desktop RCE blast radius	user compromise	least privilege capabilities + tight CSP	block release on CI
Addendum: X3 Atomic VM swap program as the canonical reference implementation

Your fastest route to “faster than Solana” is to pick one end-to-end product workload that forces the entire stack to behave: atomic cross-VM swap bundles.

How I recommend using it:

    Treat the Atomic VM swap as the golden vertical slice for:
        X3 Kernel canonical execution correctness
        Atomic Kernel admission/finality/rollback correctness
        PoAE proof generation + verification on an external chain
        GPU swarm job execution + redundancy + slashing on provable faults

Deliverable definition:

    “Swap bundle v1” becomes the reference bundle type with a standardized execution receipt schema.
    All performance claims must be tied to this workload (not synthetic tx spam).

Why this matters:

    Solana’s speed comes from tight coupling of parallelism assumptions (declared state access) + networking + crypto acceleration.
    X3’s advantage is the ability to make atomic cross-VM execution the primitive. If you can finalize atomic swap bundles faster than Solana finalizes single-chain transactions under comparable fault models, you win where it matters: complex DeFi.

If you want the roadmap even faster (shorter critical path): I would collapse the sequence to Foundation → Deterministic Parallel Proposer → GPU fast path → Atomic swap vertical slice → Flash finality cutover, and postpone Turbine-like propagation and full DA until after you have swap-bundle finality and proofs working reliably.

/// Insert development keys into the keystore for block authoring.

fn insert_dev_keys_with_seed(keystore: &KeystoreContainer, seed: &str) -> Result<(), ServiceError> {
    use sp_core::crypto::SecretStringError;

    let keystore = keystore.keystore();

    // Insert Aura key (sr25519) for block authoring
    let aura_pair =
        sp_core::sr25519::Pair::from_string(seed, None).map_err(|e: SecretStringError| {
            ServiceError::Other(format!("Failed to generate Aura keypair: {:?}", e))
        })?;
    keystore
        .insert(AURA, seed, &aura_pair.public().0)
        .map_err(|e| ServiceError::Other(format!("Failed to insert Aura key: {:?}", e)))?;

    log::info!("🔑 Inserted Aura key for block authoring");

    // Insert GRANDPA key (ed25519) for finality
    let grandpa_pair =
        sp_core::ed25519::Pair::from_string(seed, None).map_err(|e: SecretStringError| {
            ServiceError::Other(format!("Failed to generate GRANDPA keypair: {:?}", e))
        })?;
    keystore
        .insert(GRANDPA, seed, &grandpa_pair.public().0)
        .map_err(|e| ServiceError::Other(format!("Failed to insert GRANDPA key: {:?}", e)))?;

    log::info!("🔑 Inserted GRANDPA key for finality");

    Ok(())
}

    // For development chains, insert Alice's keys for block authoring
    if config.chain_spec.chain_type() == ChainType::Development {
        return insert_dev_keys_with_seed(keystore, "//Alice");
    }

    Ok(())
}

/// Start a new X3 Chain full node with complete consensus and networking
pub fn new_full(
    mut config: Configuration,
    feature_flags: NodeFeatureFlags,
) -> Result<TaskManager, ServiceError> {
    tune_transaction_pool_config(&mut config);

    let mut net_config = sc_network::config::FullNetworkConfiguration::new(&config.network);

    let grandpa_protocol_name = sc_consensus_grandpa::protocol_standard_name(
        &client.block_hash(0)?.expect("Genesis block exists; qed"),
        &config.chain_spec,

    net_config.add_notification_protocol(sc_consensus_grandpa::grandpa_peers_set_config(
        grandpa_protocol_name.clone(),
    ));

    let warp_sync = Arc::new(sc_consensus_grandpa::warp_proof::NetworkProvider::new(
        backend.clone(),
        grandpa_link.shared_authority_set().clone(),

    let (network, system_rpc_tx, tx_handler_controller, network_starter, sync_service) =
        sc_service::build_network(sc_service::BuildNetworkParams {

            client: client.clone(),
            transaction_pool: transaction_pool.clone(),
            spawn_handle: task_manager.spawn_handle(),
            import_queue,
            block_announce_validator_builder: None,
            warp_sync_params: Some(sc_service::WarpSyncParams::WithProvider(warp_sync)),

    let role = config.role.clone();

    let backoff_authoring_blocks: Option<()> = None;
    let name = config.network.node_name.clone();

    let enable_grandpa = !config.disable_grandpa;
    let prometheus_registry = config.prometheus_registry().cloned();
    let role_for_grandpa = role.clone();

    if feature_flags.enable_parallel_proposer {

    if feature_flags.enable_poh {

        );
    }
    if feature_flags.gpu_required {
        log::warn!(
            "⚠️ --gpu-required=true is set; ensure CPU fallback is not relied on by your deployment policy."
        );
    }

        let client = client.clone();
        let transaction_pool = transaction_pool.clone();

            crate::rpc::create_full(
                client.clone(),
                transaction_pool.clone(),
                deny_unsafe,
                subscription_executor,
            )
            .map_err(|e| ServiceError::Other(format!("RPC module creation failed: {:?}", e)))
        })
    };

    sc_service::spawn_tasks(sc_service::SpawnTasksParams {
        config,
        client: client.clone(),
        backend: backend.clone(),
        task_manager: &mut task_manager,
        keystore: keystore_container.keystore(),
        transaction_pool: transaction_pool.clone(),
        rpc_builder,
        network: network.clone(),
        system_rpc_tx,
        tx_handler_controller,
        sync_service: sync_service.clone(),
        telemetry: telemetry.as_mut(),

//! Lightweight integration helpers for the parallel proposer.

use crate::{DeclaredAccess, ParallelProposer, ProposalConfig, ProposalResult, TransactionMeta};
use anyhow::Result;
use std::sync::Arc;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct IntegrationConfig {
    pub proposer_config: ProposalConfig,
}

impl Default for IntegrationConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            proposer_config: ProposalConfig::default(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct IntegrationMetrics {
    pub total_submissions: u64,
    pub total_proposals: u64,
    pub failed_proposals: u64,
}

pub struct IntegrationContext {
    proposer: Arc<ParallelProposer>,
    metrics: tokio::sync::Mutex<IntegrationMetrics>,
}

impl IntegrationContext {
    pub fn new(config: IntegrationConfig) -> Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            proposer: Arc::new(ParallelProposer::new(config.proposer_config)),
            metrics: tokio::sync::Mutex::new(IntegrationMetrics::default()),
        })
    }

    pub fn proposer(&self) -> Arc<ParallelProposer> {
        self.proposer.clone()
    }

    pub async fn submit_transaction(
        &self,
        tx: TransactionMeta,
        declared_access: Option<DeclaredAccess>,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        self.proposer
            .submit_transaction_with_access(tx, declared_access)
            .await?;

        let mut metrics = self.metrics.lock().await;
        metrics.total_submissions = metrics.total_submissions.saturating_add(1);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub async fn build_next_proposal(&self) -> Result<ProposalResult> {
        let result = self.proposer.create_proposal().await;

        let mut metrics = self.metrics.lock().await;
        match &result {
            Ok(_) => {
                metrics.total_proposals = metrics.total_proposals.saturating_add(1);
            }
            Err(_) => {
                metrics.failed_proposals = metrics.failed_proposals.saturating_add(1);
            }
        }

        result
    }

    pub async fn get_metrics(&self) -> IntegrationMetrics {
        self.metrics.lock().await.clone()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn sample_tx(id: &str) -> TransactionMeta {
        TransactionMeta {
            tx_hash: id.to_string(),
            sender: "0x1".to_string(),
            receiver: "0x2".to_string(),
            value: 1,
            gas_limit: 21_000,
            gas_price: 1,
            nonce: 0,
            signature: "0123456789abcdef".to_string(),
            contract_address: Some("0xabc".to_string()),
            timestamp: 1,
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn integration_tracks_submissions_and_proposals() {
        let ctx = IntegrationContext::new(IntegrationConfig::default()).unwrap();
        ctx.submit_transaction(
            sample_tx("tx-1"),
            Some(DeclaredAccess {
                reads: vec!["r:1".to_string()],
                writes: vec!["w:1".to_string()],
            }),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();

        let _ = ctx.build_next_proposal().await.unwrap();

        let metrics = ctx.get_metrics().await;
        assert_eq!(metrics.total_submissions, 1);
        assert_eq!(metrics.total_proposals, 1);
        assert_eq!(metrics.failed_proposals, 0);
    }
}

//! Deterministic parallel proposer primitives.
//!
//! This crate is intentionally runtime-agnostic: it models deterministic scheduling,
//! shard execution, and serial fallback behavior used by a production proposer.
//! ML contention prediction is treated as a hint only.

use anyhow::{anyhow, Result};
use blake3::Hasher;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, HashMap, VecDeque};
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::sync::Mutex;
use tokio::time::Instant;

/// Transaction metadata consumed by the proposer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TransactionMeta {
    pub tx_hash: String,
    pub sender: String,
    pub receiver: String,
    pub value: u128,
    pub gas_limit: u64,
    pub gas_price: u128,
    pub nonce: u64,
    pub signature: String,
    pub contract_address: Option<String>,
    pub timestamp: u64,
}

/// Deterministic access declaration (parallel-eligible path).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DeclaredAccess {
    pub reads: Vec<String>,
    pub writes: Vec<String>,
}

/// Parallel proposal configuration.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ProposalConfig {
    pub max_parallelism: usize,
    pub contention_threshold: f64,
    pub gpu_batch_size: usize,
    pub timeout_seconds: u64,
    pub signature_batch_size: usize,
    pub min_predictor_confidence: f32,
}

impl Default for ProposalConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            max_parallelism: 16,
            contention_threshold: 0.7,
            gpu_batch_size: 256,
            timeout_seconds: 30,
            signature_batch_size: 64,
            min_predictor_confidence: 0.8,
        }
    }
}

/// Contention prediction for observability.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ContentionPrediction {
    pub tx_hash: String,
    pub contention_score: f64,
    pub conflicting_txs: Vec<String>,
    pub priority: u8,
}

/// Parallel proposal output.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ProposalResult {
    pub block_hash: String,
    pub transactions: Vec<TransactionMeta>,
    pub execution_order: Vec<usize>,

//! GPU Signature Verifier Module
//!
//! Implements high-performance signature verification using GPU acceleration
//! for parallel processing of cryptographic signatures.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Instant;

use tokio::sync::mpsc;

/// Signature verification configuration
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct VerifierConfig {
    pub batch_size: usize,
    pub timeout_seconds: u64,
    pub max_retries: u8,
    pub gpu_device_id: u32,
    pub enable_profiling: bool,
}

impl Default for VerifierConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            batch_size: 256,
            timeout_seconds: 30,
            max_retries: 3,
            gpu_device_id: 0,
            enable_profiling: false,
        }
    }
}

/// Signature verification result
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct VerificationResult {
    pub signature_id: String,
    pub verified: bool,
    pub verification_time_ms: f64,
    pub error_message: Option<String>,
    pub batch_id: u32,
}

/// Batch verification statistics
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BatchStats {
    pub batch_id: u32,
    pub total_signatures: usize,
    pub successful_verifications: usize,
    pub failed_verifications: usize,
    pub average_time_ms: f64,
    pub throughput_sps: f64,
}

/// GPU signature verifier core
pub struct GPUSignatureVerifier {
    config: VerifierConfig,
    gpu_context: Arc<Mutex<GPUContext>>,
    stats: Arc<Mutex<VerificationStats>>,
    retry_queue: Arc<Mutex<Vec<VerificationRequest>>>,
}

impl GPUSignatureVerifier {
    /// Create a new GPU signature verifier
    pub fn new(config: VerifierConfig) -> Self {
        Self {
            config,
            gpu_context: Arc::new(Mutex::new(GPUContext::new(config.gpu_device_id))),
            stats: Arc::new(Mutex::new(VerificationStats::new())),
            retry_queue: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new())),
        }
    }

    /// Verify a single signature
    pub async fn verify_signature(&self, signature: &str, data: &[u8]) -> Result<VerificationResult> {
        let request = VerificationRequest {
            id: generate_signature_id(),
            signature: signature.to_string(),
            data: data.to_vec(),
            attempts: 0,
        };

        self.process_request(request).await
    }

    /// Verify multiple signatures in parallel
    pub async fn verify_signatures(&self, signatures: Vec<(&str, &[u8])>) -> Result<Vec<VerificationResult>> {
        let mut results = Vec::with_capacity(signatures.len());
        let mut requests = Vec::with_capacity(signatures.len());

        for (signature, data) in signatures {
            let request = VerificationRequest {
                id: generate_signature_id(),
                signature: signature.to_string(),
                data: data.to_vec(),
                attempts: 0,
            };
            requests.push(request);
        }

        // Process in batches
        for batch in requests.chunks(self.config.batch_size) {
            let batch_results = self.process_batch(batch).await?;
            results.extend(batch_results);
        }

        Ok(results)
    }

    /// Process verification request with retry logic
    async fn process_request(&self, request: VerificationRequest) -> Result<VerificationResult> {
        let mut attempts = 0;
        let mut result = None;

        while attempts <= self.config.max_retries {
            let start_time = Instant::now();
            let verification = self.gpu_context.lock().await.verify(&request).await;

            let elapsed_time = start_time.elapsed().as_millis() as f64;
            let verified = verification.is_ok();

            // Update stats
            self.update_stats(verified, elapsed_time).await;

            if verification.is_ok() {
                result = Some(VerificationResult {
                    signature_id: request.id.clone(),
                    verified: true,
                    verification_time_ms: elapsed_time,
                    error_message: None,
                    batch_id: 0,
                });
                break;
            } else {
                attempts += 1;
                if attempts > self.config.max_retries {
                    result = Some(VerificationResult {
                        signature_id: request.id.clone(),
                        verified: false,
                        verification_time_ms: elapsed_time,
                        error_message: Some(verification.err().unwrap_or("Unknown error".to_string())),
                        batch_id: 0,
                    });
                }
            }
        }

        Ok(result.unwrap())
    }

    async fn update_stats(&self, verified: bool, time_ms: f64) {
        let mut stats = self.stats.lock().await;
        stats.total_verifications += 1;

        } else {

        let mut stats = self.stats.lock().await;
        stats.clear();
    }
}

/// GPU context for signature verification
struct GPUContext {
    device_id: u32,
    // GPU resources would be managed here
}

impl GPUContext {
    fn new(device_id: u32) -> Self {
        Self { device_id }
    }

    async fn verify(&mut self, request: &VerificationRequest) -> Result<()> {
        // Simulate GPU verification
        if Self::simulate_verification(&request.signature, &request.data) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(anyhow!("Verification failed"))
        }
    }

    fn simulate_verification(signature: &str, data: &[u8]) -> bool {
        // Simple validation - in real implementation this would use GPU acceleration
        !signature.is_empty() && signature.len() > 64 && data.len() > 0
    }
}

/// Verification request structure
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct VerificationRequest {
    id: String,
    signature: String,
    data: Vec<u8>,
    attempts: u8,
}

/// Global verification statistics
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct VerificationStats {
    pub total_verifications: usize,
    pub successful_verifications: usize,
    pub failed_verifications: usize,
    pub total_time_ms: f64,
    pub average_time_ms: f64,
    pub next_batch_id: u32,
    pub batch_stats: Vec<BatchStats>,
}

impl VerificationStats {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            total_verifications: 0,
            successful_verifications: 0,
            failed_verifications: 0,
            total_time_ms: 0.0,
            average_time_ms: 0.0,
            next_batch_id: 1,
            batch_stats: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.total_verifications = 0;
        self.successful_verifications = 0;
        self.failed_verifications = 0;
        self.total_time_ms = 0.0;
        self.average_time_ms = 0.0;
        self.next_batch_id = 1;
        self.batch_stats.clear();
    }
}

/// Generate unique signature ID
fn generate_signature_id() -> String {
    format!("{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4())
}

fn insert_dev_keys_with_seed(keystore: &KeystoreContainer, seed: &str) -> Result<(), ServiceError> {
    use sp_core::crypto::SecretStringError;

    let keystore = keystore.keystore();

    // Insert Aura key (sr25519) for block authoring
    let aura_pair =
        sp_core::sr25519::Pair::from_string(seed, None).map_err(|e: SecretStringError| {
            ServiceError::Other(format!("Failed to generate Aura keypair: {:?}", e))
        })?;
    keystore
        .insert(AURA, seed, &aura_pair.public().0)
        .map_err(|e| ServiceError::Other(format!("Failed to insert Aura key: {:?}", e)))?;

    log::info!("🔑 Inserted Aura key for block authoring");

    // Insert GRANDPA key (ed25519) for finality
    let grandpa_pair =
        sp_core::ed25519::Pair::from_string(seed, None).map_err(|e: SecretStringError| {
            ServiceError::Other(format!("Failed to generate GRANDPA keypair: {:?}", e))
        })?;
    keystore
        .insert(GRANDPA, seed, &grandpa_pair.public().0)
        .map_err(|e| ServiceError::Other(format!("Failed to insert GRANDPA key: {:?}", e)))?;

    log::info!("🔑 Inserted GRANDPA key for finality");

    Ok(())
}

+        use gpu_sig_verifier::{GPUSignatureVerifier, VerifierConfig};
+        use tokio::time::{interval, Duration};
+
+        let verifier = GPUSignatureVerifier::new(VerifierConfig {
+            batch_size: 32,
+            enable_profiling: true,
+            ..VerifierConfig::default()
+        });
+        let mut ticker = interval(Duration::from_secs(30));
+
+        loop {
+            ticker.tick().await;
+            let started_at = Instant::now();
+
+            let mut signatures: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(32);
+            let mut payloads: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::with_capacity(32);
+            for i in 0..32u64 {
+                signatures.push(format!("{:0>80}", i));
+                payloads.push(format!("shadow-data-{}", i).into_bytes());
+            }
+            let inputs: Vec<(&str, &[u8])> = signatures
+                .iter()
+                .zip(payloads.iter())
+                .map(|(sig, data)| (sig.as_str(), data.as_slice()))
+                .collect();
+
+            match verifier.verify_signatures(inputs).await {
+                Ok(results) => {
+                    let failures = results.iter().filter(|r| !r.verified).count();
+                    let elapsed_ms = started_at.elapsed().as_millis();
+                    if failures > 0 {
+                        log::warn!(
+                            "GPU validation shadow batch completed with {} failures in {}ms",
+                            failures,
+                            elapsed_ms
+                        );
+                        if gpu_required {
+                            log::error!(
+                                "--gpu-required=true set but GPU validation batch reported failures"
+                            );
+                        }
+                    } else {
+                        log::info!(
+                            "GPU validation shadow batch ok ({} signatures in {}ms)",
+                            results.len(),
+                            elapsed_ms
+                        );
+                    }
+                }
+                Err(err) => {
+                    log::warn!("GPU validation shadow batch failed: {}", err);
+                    if gpu_required {
+                        log::error!("--gpu-required=true set but GPU validation failed");
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    });
+}

fn tuned_transaction_pool_options(
    mut options: sc_transaction_pool::Options,
) -> sc_transaction_pool::Options {
    options.ready.count = options.ready.count.max(TX_POOL_READY_COUNT);
    options.future.count = options.future.count.max(TX_POOL_FUTURE_COUNT);
    options.ready.total_bytes = options.ready.total_bytes.max(TX_POOL_TOTAL_BYTES);
    options.future.total_bytes = options.future.total_bytes.max(TX_POOL_TOTAL_BYTES);
    options.ban_time = Duration::from_secs(TX_POOL_BAN_TIME_SECS);
    options
}

/// Apply the tuned limits to a runtime configuration before the pool is built.
pub fn tune_transaction_pool_config(config: &mut Configuration) {
    config.transaction_pool = tuned_transaction_pool_options(config.transaction_pool.clone());
}

/// Create partial components for X3 Chain node
///
/// Returns the common components needed by various subcommands (benchmarking, export, etc.)
pub fn new_partial(
    config: &Configuration,
) -> Result<
    PartialComponents<
        FullClient,
        FullBackend,
        SelectChain,
        sc_consensus::DefaultImportQueue<Block, FullClient>,
        sc_transaction_pool::FullPool<Block, FullClient>,
        (
            sc_consensus_grandpa::GrandpaBlockImport<FullBackend, Block, FullClient, SelectChain>,
            sc_consensus_grandpa::LinkHalf<Block, FullClient, SelectChain>,
            Option<Telemetry>,
        ),
    >,
    ServiceError,
> {
    // Set up telemetry if endpoints are configured
    let telemetry = config
        .telemetry_endpoints
        .clone()
        .filter(|x| !x.is_empty())
        .map(|endpoints| -> Result<_, sc_telemetry::Error> {
            let worker = TelemetryWorker::new(16)?;
            let telemetry = worker.handle().new_telemetry(endpoints);
            Ok((worker, telemetry))
        })
        .transpose()?;

    // Create executor
    let executor = Executor::new(config.wasm_method, None, 8, 64);

    // Build partial components
    let (client, backend, keystore_container, task_manager) =
        sc_service::new_full_parts::<Block, RuntimeApi, _>(
            &config,
            telemetry.as_ref().map(|(_, telemetry)| telemetry.handle()),
            executor,
        )?;

    // For dev chains or when X3_DEV_SEED is set, insert keys for block authoring.
    maybe_insert_dev_keys(config, &keystore_container)?;

    options.ban_time = Duration::from_secs(TX_POOL_BAN_TIME_SECS);
    options
}

/// Apply the tuned limits to a runtime configuration before the pool is built.
pub fn tune_transaction_pool_config(config: &mut Configuration) {
    config.transaction_pool = tuned_transaction_pool_options(config.transaction_pool.clone());
}

fn spawn_gpu_validation_shadow(task_manager: &TaskManager, gpu_required: bool) {
    task_manager
        .spawn_handle()
        .spawn("gpu-validation-shadow", None, async move {
            use gpu_sig_verifier::{GPUSignatureVerifier, VerifierConfig};
            use tokio::time::{interval, Duration as TokioDuration};

            let verifier = GPUSignatureVerifier::new(VerifierConfig {
                batch_size: 32,
                enable_profiling: true,
                ..VerifierConfig::default()
            });
            let mut ticker = interval(TokioDuration::from_secs(30));

            loop {
                ticker.tick().await;
                let started_at = Instant::now();

                let mut signatures: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(32);
                let mut payloads: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::with_capacity(32);
                for i in 0..32u64 {
                    signatures.push(format!("{:0>80}", i));
                    payloads.push(format!("shadow-data-{}", i).into_bytes());
                }
                let inputs: Vec<(&str, &[u8])> = signatures
                    .iter()
                    .zip(payloads.iter())
                    .map(|(sig, data)| (sig.as_str(), data.as_slice()))
                    .collect();

                match verifier.verify_signatures(inputs).await {
                    Ok(results) => {
                        let failures = results.iter().filter(|r| !r.verified).count();
                        let elapsed_ms = started_at.elapsed().as_millis();
                        if failures > 0 {
                            log::warn!(
                                "GPU validation shadow batch completed with {} failures in {}ms",
                                failures,
                                elapsed_ms
                            );
                            if gpu_required {
                                log::error!(
                                    "--gpu-required=true set but GPU validation batch reported failures"
                                );
                            }
                        } else {
                            log::info!(
                                "GPU validation shadow batch ok ({} signatures in {}ms)",
                                results.len(),
                                elapsed_ms
                            );
                        }
                    }
                    Err(err) => {
                        log::warn!("GPU validation shadow batch failed: {}", err);
                        if gpu_required {
                            log::error!("--gpu-required=true set but GPU validation failed");
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        });
}

- content: `//! Flash Finality scaffolding (shadow-mode).
//!
//! This crate provides message formats and a lightweight voter task stub.
//! It does not alter consensus unless explicitly wired into block import.

#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]

use parity_scale_codec::{Decode, Encode};
use sp_runtime::RuntimeDebug;
use tokio::time::{interval, Duration};

/// Flash Finality proposal message.
#[derive(Clone, Encode, Decode, RuntimeDebug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Proposal {
    pub block_hash: [u8; 32],
    pub slot: u64,
    pub round: u64,
    pub leader_id: [u8; 32],
    pub leader_sig: Vec<u8>,
}

/// Flash Finality vote message.
#[derive(Clone, Encode, Decode, RuntimeDebug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Vote {
    pub block_hash: [u8; 32],
    pub slot: u64,
    pub round: u64,
    pub voter_id: [u8; 32],
    pub voter_sig: Vec<u8>,
}

/// Flash Finality certificate (multisig tuples).
#[derive(Clone, Encode, Decode, RuntimeDebug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Certificate {
    pub block_hash: [u8; 32],
    pub slot: u64,
    pub round: u64,
    pub signers: Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>,
}

/// Lightweight block import wrapper placeholder.
///
/// This struct is intentionally minimal; it can be expanded to implement
/// `sc_consensus::BlockImport` once the gadget is fully integrated.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct FlashFinalityBlockImport<I> {
    inner: I,
}

impl<I> FlashFinalityBlockImport<I> {
    pub fn new(inner: I) -> Self {
        Self { inner }
    }

    pub fn inner(&self) -> &I {
        &self.inner
    }
}

/// Shadow-mode voter task stub.
///
/// This periodically emits logs to validate scheduling, without changing finality.
pub async fn run_flash_finality_voter_shadow() {
    let mut ticker = interval(Duration::from_secs(5));
    loop {
        ticker.tick().await;
        tracing::info!("Flash Finality shadow voter tick");
    }
}
`

- content: `//! Parallel proposer adapter for Aura.
//!
//! This is an active wiring hook that wraps an inner proposer environment.
//! It currently delegates to the inner proposer while providing a stable
//! place to integrate deterministic parallel scheduling in the next step.

use futures::future::BoxFuture;
use sp_consensus::{Environment, Proposer};
use sp_runtime::traits::Block as BlockT;
use std::marker::PhantomData;

pub struct ParallelProposerFactory<E, Block>
where
    Block: BlockT,
    E: Environment<Block>,
{
    inner: E,
    _marker: PhantomData<Block>,
}

impl<E, Block> ParallelProposerFactory<E, Block>
where
    Block: BlockT,
    E: Environment<Block>,
{
    pub fn new(inner: E) -> Self {
        Self {
            inner,
            _marker: PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

pub struct ParallelProposerAdapter<P, Block>
where
    Block: BlockT,
    P: Proposer<Block>,
{
    inner: P,
    _marker: PhantomData<Block>,
}

impl<P, Block> ParallelProposerAdapter<P, Block>
where
    Block: BlockT,
    P: Proposer<Block>,
{
    pub fn new(inner: P) -> Self {
        Self {
            inner,
            _marker: PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

impl<E, Block> Environment<Block> for ParallelProposerFactory<E, Block>
where
    Block: BlockT,
    E: Environment<Block> + Send,
    E::Proposer: Proposer<Block> + Send,
    E::CreateProposerFuture: Send + 'static,
{
    type Proposer = ParallelProposerAdapter<E::Proposer, Block>;
    type Error = E::Error;
    type CreateProposerFuture = BoxFuture<'static, Result<Self::Proposer, Self::Error>>;

    fn init(&mut self, parent_header: &Block::Header) -> Self::CreateProposerFuture {
        let mut inner = &mut self.inner;
        Box::pin(async move {
            let proposer = inner.init(parent_header).await?;
            Ok(ParallelProposerAdapter::new(proposer))
        })
    }
}

impl<P, Block> Proposer<Block> for ParallelProposerAdapter<P, Block>
where
    Block: BlockT,
    P: Proposer<Block> + Send,
    P::Error: Send,
    P::CreateProposalFuture: Send,
    P::Proposal: Send,
{
    type Error = P::Error;
    type Proposal = P::Proposal;
    type CreateProposalFuture = P::CreateProposalFuture;

    fn propose(
        &self,
        inherent_data: sp_inherents::InherentData,
        inherent_digests: sp_runtime::generic::Digest,
        max_duration: std::time::Duration,
        record_proof: sp_consensus::RecordProof,
    ) -> Self::CreateProposalFuture {
        // TODO: integrate deterministic parallel scheduling before delegating.
        self.inner
            .propose(inherent_data, inherent_digests, max_duration, record_proof)
    }
}
`

/// Default block size limit in bytes used by [`Proposer`].
///
/// Can be overwritten by [`ProposerFactory::set_default_block_size_limit`].
///
/// Be aware that there is also an upper packet size on what the networking code
/// will accept. If the block doesn't fit in such a package, it can not be
/// transferred to other nodes.
pub const DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE_LIMIT: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024 + 512;

const DEFAULT_SOFT_DEADLINE_PERCENT: Percent = Percent::from_percent(50);

/// [`Proposer`] factory.

	/// limit will be used.

	/// Soft deadline percentage of hard deadline.
	///
	/// The value is used to compute soft deadline during block production.
	/// The soft deadline indicates where we should stop attempting to add transactions
	/// to the block, which exhaust resources. After soft deadline is reached,
	/// we switch to a fixed-amount mode, in which after we see `MAX_SKIPPED_TRANSACTIONS`
	/// transactions which exhaust resrouces, we will conclude that the block is full.
	soft_deadline_percent: Percent,
	telemetry: Option<TelemetryHandle>,
	/// When estimating the block size, should the proof be included?
	include_proof_in_block_size_estimation: bool,
	/// phantom member to pin the `Backend`/`ProofRecording` type.
	_phantom: PhantomData<(B, PR)>,
}

/// If the block is full we will attempt to push at most
/// this number of transactions before quitting for real.
/// It allows us to increase block utilization.
const MAX_SKIPPED_TRANSACTIONS: usize = 8;

impl<A, B, Block, C, PR> Proposer<B, Block, C, A, PR>

	) -> Result<Proposal<Block, backend::TransactionFor<B, Block>, PR::Proof>, sp_blockchain::Error>
	{
		let propose_with_timer = time::Instant::now();
		let mut block_builder =
			self.client.new_block_at(self.parent_hash, inherent_digests, PR::ENABLED)?;

		self.apply_inherents(&mut block_builder, inherent_data)?;

		// TODO call `after_inherents` and check if we should apply extrinsincs here
		// <https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/pull/14275/>

		let block_timer = time::Instant::now();
		let end_reason =
			self.apply_extrinsics(&mut block_builder, deadline, block_size_limit).await?;
		let (block, storage_changes, proof) = block_builder.build()?.into_inner();
		let block_took = block_timer.elapsed();

		let proof =
			PR::into_proof(proof).map_err(|e| sp_blockchain::Error::Application(Box::new(e)))?;

		self.print_summary(&block, end_reason, block_took, propose_with_timer.elapsed());
		Ok(Proposal { block, proof, storage_changes })
	}

	) -> Result<(), sp_blockchain::Error> {
		let create_inherents_start = time::Instant::now();

				Ok(_) => {},
			}
		}
		Ok(())
	}

/// The proposer logic.
pub struct Proposer<B, Block: BlockT, C, A: TransactionPool, PR> {
	spawn_handle: Box<dyn SpawnNamed>,
	client: Arc<C>,
	parent_hash: Block::Hash,
	parent_number: <<Block as BlockT>::Header as HeaderT>::Number,
	transaction_pool: Arc<A>,
	now: Box<dyn Fn() -> time::Instant + Send + Sync>,
	metrics: PrometheusMetrics,
	default_block_size_limit: usize,
	include_proof_in_block_size_estimation: bool,
	soft_deadline_percent: Percent,
	telemetry: Option<TelemetryHandle>,
	_phantom: PhantomData<(B, PR)>,
}

/// Transaction pool status.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct PoolStatus {
	/// Number of transactions in the ready queue.
	pub ready: usize,
	/// Sum of bytes of ready transaction encodings.
	pub ready_bytes: usize,
	/// Number of transactions in the future queue.
	pub future: usize,
	/// Sum of bytes of ready transaction encodings.
	pub future_bytes: usize,
}

impl PoolStatus {
	/// Returns true if the are no transactions in the pool.
	pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
		self.ready == 0 && self.future == 0
	}
}

/// Possible transaction status events.
///
/// This events are being emitted by `TransactionPool` watchers,
/// which are also exposed over RPC.
///
/// The status events can be grouped based on their kinds as:
/// 1. Entering/Moving within the pool:
/// 		- `Future`
/// 		- `Ready`
/// 2. Inside `Ready` queue:
/// 		- `Broadcast`
/// 3. Leaving the pool:
/// 		- `InBlock`
/// 		- `Invalid`
/// 		- `Usurped`
/// 		- `Dropped`
/// 	4. Re-entering the pool:
/// 		- `Retracted`
/// 	5. Block finalized:
/// 		- `Finalized`
/// 		- `FinalityTimeout`
///
/// The events will always be received in the order described above, however
/// there might be cases where transactions alternate between `Future` and `Ready`
/// pool, and are `Broadcast` in the meantime.
///
/// There is also only single event causing the transaction to leave the pool.
/// I.e. only one of the listed ones should be triggered.
///
/// Note that there are conditions that may cause transactions to reappear in the pool.
/// 1. Due to possible forks, the transaction that ends up being in included
/// in one block, may later re-enter the pool or be marked as invalid.
/// 2. Transaction `Dropped` at one point, may later re-enter the pool if some other
/// transactions are removed.
/// 3. `Invalid` transaction may become valid at some point in the future.
/// (Note that runtimes are encouraged to use `UnknownValidity` to inform the pool about
/// such case).
/// 4. `Retracted` transactions might be included in some next block.
///
/// The stream is considered finished only when either `Finalized` or `FinalityTimeout`
/// event is triggered. You are however free to unsubscribe from notifications at any point.
/// The first one will be emitted when the block, in which transaction was included gets
/// finalized. The `FinalityTimeout` event will be emitted when the block did not reach finality
/// within 512 blocks. This either indicates that finality is not available for your chain,
/// or that finality gadget is lagging behind. If you choose to wait for finality longer, you can
/// re-subscribe for a particu…66 tokens truncated… ready queue.

	/// Maximum number of finality watchers has been reached,

	fn ready_transaction(&self, hash: &TxHash<Self>) -> Option<Arc<Self::InPoolTransaction>>;

/// The implementation is then allowed, for performance reasons, to change the elements
/// returned next, by e.g.  skipping elements that are known to depend on the reported
/// transaction, which yields them invalid as well.
pub trait ReadyTransactions: Iterator {

+const MAX_READY_TXS: usize = 1024;
+const MAX_SKIPPED_TRANSACTIONS: usize = 8;
+
+pub struct ParallelProposerFactory<A, B, C, PR> {
+    spawn_handle: Box<dyn SpawnNamed>,
+    client: Arc<C>,
+    transaction_pool: Arc<A>,
+    default_block_size_limit: usize,
+    soft_deadline_percent: Percent,
+    include_proof_in_block_size_estimation: bool,
+    _phantom: PhantomData<(B, PR)>,
+}
+
+impl<A, B, C> ParallelProposerFactory<A, B, C, DisableProofRecording> {
+    pub fn new(
+        spawn_handle: impl SpawnNamed + 'static,
+        client: Arc<C>,
+        transaction_pool: Arc<A>,
+        _prometheus: Option<&prometheus_endpoint::Registry>,
+        _telemetry: Option<sc_telemetry::TelemetryHandle>,
+    ) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            spawn_handle: Box::new(spawn_handle),
+            client,
+            transaction_pool,
+            default_block_size_limit: DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE_LIMIT,
+            soft_deadline_percent: DEFAULT_SOFT_DEADLINE_PERCENT,
+            include_proof_in_block_size_estimation: false,
+            _phantom: PhantomData,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl<A, B, Block, C, PR> Environment<Block> for ParallelProposerFactory<A, B, C, PR>
+where
+    A: TransactionPool<Block = Block> + 'static,
+    B: backend::Backend<Block> + Send + Sync + 'static,
+    Block: BlockT,

+{
+    type CreateProposerFuture = future::Ready<Result<Self::Proposer, Self::Error>>;
+    type Proposer = ParallelProposer<B, Block, C, A, PR>;
+    type Error = sp_blockchain::Error;
+
+    fn init(&mut self, parent_header: &<Block as BlockT>::Header) -> Self::CreateProposerFuture {
+        let proposer = ParallelProposer {
+            spawn_handle: self.spawn_handle.clone(),
+            client: self.client.clone(),
+            parent_hash: parent_header.hash(),
+            parent_number: *parent_header.number(),
+            transaction_pool: self.transaction_pool.clone(),
+            default_block_size_limit: self.default_block_size_limit,
+            soft_deadline_percent: self.soft_deadline_percent,
+            include_proof_in_block_size_estimation: self.include_proof_in_block_size_estimation,
+            _phantom: PhantomData,
+        };
+
+        future::ready(Ok(proposer))
+    }

+pub struct ParallelProposer<B, Block: BlockT, C, A: TransactionPool, PR> {

+    client: Arc<C>,

+    parent_number: <<Block as BlockT>::Header as HeaderT>::Number,
+    transaction_pool: Arc<A>,
+    default_block_size_limit: usize,

+    soft_deadline_percent: Percent,

+}

+impl<A, B, Block, C, PR> sp_consensus::Proposer<Block> for ParallelProposer<B, Block, C, A, PR>
+where
+    A: TransactionPool<Block = Block> + 'static,
+    B: backend::Backend<Block> + Send + Sync + 'static,

+    fn propose(

+        inherent_digests: Digest,

+        let spawn_handle = self.spawn_handle.clone();

+        spawn_handle.spawn_blocking(

+            None,

+                let res = self

+                if tx.send(res).is_err() {

+impl<A, B, Block, C, PR> ParallelProposer<B, Block, C, A, PR>

+        self.apply_inherents(&mut block_builder, inherent_data)?;
+
+        let end_reason =
+            self.apply_extrinsics_parallel(&mut block_builder, deadline, block_size_limit)

+
+        let (block, storage_changes, proof) = block_builder.build()?.into_inner();
+        let proof =
+            PR::into_proof(proof).map_err(|e| sp_blockchain::Error::Application(Box::new(e)))?;
+
+        debug!("Parallel proposer finished: {:?}", end_reason);

+            block,
+            proof,
+            storage_changes,
+        })

+    fn apply_inherents(

+                    warn!("Dropping non-mandatory inherent from overweight block.")

+                Err(ApplyExtrinsicFailed(Validity(e))) if e.was_mandatory() => {

+                Err(e) => {
+                    pending_iterator.report_invalid(pending_tx);
+                    debug!("Invalid transaction {:?}: {}", pending_tx_hash, e);
+                }
+            }
+        }
+
+        Ok(EndReason::NoMoreTransactions)
+    }
+
+    fn build_deterministic_plan(
+        &self,
+        pending: &[Arc<A::InPoolTransaction>],
+    ) -> Vec<usize> {
+        let mut shards: Vec<Shard> = Vec::new();
+        let mut serial_fallback = Vec::new();
+
+        for (idx, tx) in pending.iter().enumerate() {
+            let access = extract_declared_access(tx.data());
+            let Some(access) = access else {
+                serial_fallback.push(idx);
+                continue;
+            };
+
+            if access.reads.is_empty() && access.writes.is_empty() {
+                serial_fallback.push(idx);
+                continue;
+            }
+
+            let target = find_conflict_free_shard(&shards, &access)
+                .unwrap_or_else(|| shards.len());
+
+            if target == shards.len() {
+                shards.push(Shard::default());
+            }
+
+            add_to_shard(&mut shards[target], idx, &access);
+        }
+
+        let mut ordered = Vec::with_capacity(pending.len());
+        for shard in shards {
+            ordered.extend(shard.tx_indices);
+        }
+        ordered.extend(serial_fallback);
+        ordered
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Default)]
+struct Shard {
+    tx_indices: Vec<usize>,
+    reads: BTreeSet<Vec<u8>>,
+    writes: BTreeSet<Vec<u8>>,
+}
+
+fn extract_declared_access<T>(_xt: &T) -> Option<DeclaredAccess> {
+    // TODO: decode signed extension access list for parallel-eligible extrinsics.
+    None
+}
+
+fn find_conflict_free_shard(shards: &[Shard], access: &DeclaredAccess) -> Option<usize> {
+    let reads: BTreeSet<Vec<u8>> = access.reads.iter().map(|v| v.as_bytes().to_vec()).collect();
+    let writes: BTreeSet<Vec<u8>> = access.writes.iter().map(|v| v.as_bytes().to_vec()).collect();
+
+    for (idx, shard) in shards.iter().enumerate() {
+        let write_write = !writes.is_disjoint(&shard.writes);
+        let write_read = !writes.is_disjoint(&shard.reads);
+        let read_write = !reads.is_disjoint(&shard.writes);
+        if !(write_write || write_read || read_write) {
+            return Some(idx);
+        }
+    }
+    None
+}
+
+fn add_to_shard(shard: &mut Shard, tx_idx: usize, access: &DeclaredAccess) {
+    shard.tx_indices.push(tx_idx);
+    shard
+        .reads
+        .extend(access.reads.iter().map(|v| v.as_bytes().to_vec()));
+    shard
+        .writes
+        .extend(access.writes.iter().map(|v| v.as_bytes().to_vec()));
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug)]
+enum EndReason {
+    NoTransactions,
+    NoMoreTransactions,
+    HitDeadline,
+    HitBlockSizeLimit,
+    HitBlockWeightLimit,
+}
